questions: Is the goal to sort P into strictly increasing order (1,2,...,N), or is any order (like non-decreasing) acceptable?
When swapping P_i and P_{i+1} with cost i, does the cost refer to the index i before the swap, or does it change if the elements move to new positions?
Are we allowed to perform swaps in any order, or must we follow a specific algorithm (like bubble sort) to minimize cost?
Does 'total cost required to sort P in order' mean the minimum possible total cost over all sequences of swaps that result in a sorted permutation?
If multiple swap sequences achieve sorting, are we to output the cost of any valid sequence, or specifically the minimum?
Is the cost i an absolute value, or can it be negative? The constraints don't specify, but i is between 1 and N-1.
Can we choose the same i multiple times consecutively, or are there restrictions on repeated swaps?
Does the cost accumulate additively, or are there other operations (like combining costs) that affect total?
